title: Rebind IFX to V4 Guards 1.1.6 with successor bundle 0.4.4 (I1; IFX-V4-002, IFX-V4-003)
goal: Make IFX consume V4 Guards 1.1.6 from von12549/Guard through successor bundle 0.4.4, human review, composition, parity and P10.3 successor rehearsal, and close IFX-V4-002 (Linux timeout) and IFX-V4-003 (C6c Linux installer path) through C6c successor harness changes.
acceptanceCriteria: The 1.1.6 archive, install receipt and package hash match the published Guard release identities.
Bundle 0.4.4 differs from 0.4.3 only as the Plan allows; C6c Windows certification and controls pass and the Linux leg passes with the release-archive installer on container-native storage.
Explicit human acceptance binds the exact 0.4.4 review packet and a production review bound to the 1.1.6 archive.
The composed 1.1.6 + 0.4.4 installation verifies, the clean Pre passes and the deliberate violation blocks.
Parity replays 52 of 52 cases with zero gaps, the same 15 strengthenings and no semantic drift.
The P10.3 successor rehearsal passes with every negative control, including the source-path installer control.
V3 contexts, V3/V3_ifx source, IFX workflows and rulesets are unchanged.
risks: The accepted 1.1.5 scripts could be edited instead of succeeded.
A module timeout could be raised without measuring the native Linux duration first.
The Linux leg could still read the Target over the Windows bind mount.
Expiring C6 evidence locks could be extended instead of regenerated.
A consumer rebinding could be misrepresented as activation or P10.GATE.
decisions: Build successor bundle 0.4.4 for base 1.1.6 instead of editing the accepted 0.4.3 tuple.
Take the Linux installer from the hash-verified release archive, never from docs/guards/v4.
Measure ifx-database-evidence on container-native storage before any module change; a module change needs an operator decision.
Keep Linux a non-blocking C6c assessment; making it blocking belongs to P10.GATE.
